title: Civil Procedure
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze personal jurisdiction, subject-matter jurisdiction, venue, the Erie doctrine, pleading, joinder, discovery, summary judgment, trial and judgment, appeals, and claim and issue preclusion under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.
primary_reading: Cornell LII: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

weeks.1: Personal jurisdiction: from Pennoyer to International Shoe
weeks.3: Subject-matter jurisdiction: federal questions and diversity

blocks.deliverable: Analyze personal jurisdiction over an out-of-state company.
Decide whether a case belongs in federal court.
Apply Erie to a statute-of-limitations conflict.
Week 7 midterm; evaluate a complaint against the plausibility standard.
Draft a discovery plan and decide a summary judgment motion.
Analyze preclusion in a two-lawsuit problem.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Litigation file: from supplied facts, decide where to sue and why, draft a complaint with its jurisdictional allegations, and write a memo on likely motions to dismiss and a discovery plan.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
